findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a partially cooked chicken breast stored in the drawer cooler in direct contact with raw chicken breast. PIC was made aware and the pan with partially cooked chicken and raw chicken was removed from the cook line and voluntarily discarded. Par cooking is not a standard practice at this facility and the PIC was unaware of when or why the chicken was partially cooked.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.[P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the shelving in the walk-in cooler to be heavily soiled with debris and microbial growth. findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the salad station cooler and sandwich cooler 1 fail to hold foods at a temperature of 41F or less. The inspector observed shredded cheese in the salad station cooler measure 44.3F with a probe thermometer, and sliced tomato in the sandwich cooler 1 measure 47.9F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the coolers have a history of complications and replacement coolers have been ordered. In the meantime, all TCS foods in these two coolers have been converted to either time as a control or an ice bath for cold holding. The PIC is responsible for monitoring cold holding in these areas. Ensure proper monitoring is conducted to maintain a temperature of 41F or less for all TCS foods in the coolers until replacements are delivered.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the mop head stored directly on the floor by the mop sink. This violation was previously noted in September 2024, March 2025, June 2025, and February 2026, and March 2026. This storage method does not allow for proper drip drying. The inspector recommended propping the mop against the wall of the mop sink with the mop head upright to drip dry, or storing the mop in the straining basin of the bucket rather than the basin of the bucket or the floor. A follow-up will be conducted on April 15, 2026 to ensure proper mop storage is being conducted in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Upon arrival, PIC informed inspectors that the dish machine was also programmed for chemical sanitization, but the machine tested 0ppm with a chlorine test strip twice. The dish machine was observed with a final rinse temperature of 150.4F with the dish puck. The inspectors informed the PIC that the sanitizer bucket was empty and therefore not supplying the machine with chlorine for sanitization. The final rinse temperature observed is also insufficient to achieve sanitation. The chemical bucket was replaced during the inspection, but the machine failed to pull the sanitizer through the system via the pump. A follow-up is scheduled for 11/21/2025 to ensure Ecolab services and repairs the dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the lactic acid sanitizer dispenser in the dish room to measure 0ppm lactic acid with a test strip. The dispenser’s sanitizer source jug was observed to be nearly empty. If the tubing is not long enough, the sanitizer dispenser can fail before the container is fully emptied. Ensure staff are testing the dispensed sanitizer frequently and monitoring the fill level on the chemical jug. The PIC was informed of the issue and the jug was replaced, measuring 700ppm lactic acid.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED.

findings.comment: Observed an apparent lack of communication between Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM’s) on staff. Today’s CFPM seemed unaware of the service needed on the dish machine and was allowing staff to use machine for sanitization. Communication in the kitchen is vital for enabling proper food handling and avoiding cross-contamination. Ensure CFPM’s on staff are effectively communicating information regarding food safety to all staff in the kitchen. This violation will be spot checked along with the follow-up scheduled on 3/13/2025 regarding the dish machine.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
Observed the lactic acid sanitizer from the dispenser to be at 170 ppm. The facility has called the company to come out and adjust the sanitizer dispenser. This sanitizer is used for sanitizer buckets.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 
Observed a bag of food thawing in a prep sink of standing water. The water faucet was turned on. Thaw foods properly according to one of the methods listed above.

findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.
